name: embarrassment
quote: I spilled the drink on my date.
description: Dismay about how an action may have brought unwanted negative attention from others with a prediction of a short-term loss of social status.
perceptions: I did something to bring minor negative attention to myself.
I did not want this type of attention.
The impact is uncomfortable but should be relatively short-lived.
examples: Wearing casual clothes to an important formal event.

guidance.description: Nearly everyone experiences embarrassment from time to time. Whether you’ve said something you didn’t mean, made a mistake, or had an awkward social moment, you aren’t alone. Embarrassment can make you feel self-conscious and often involves feeling out of place, shameful, or uncomfortable in a social situation. Although you may not be able to avoid embarrassing situations entirely, there are tips you can follow to help move on from embarrassing moments.

comparisons.description: 'Embarrassment' is a sense that you've broken a minor rule that you did not want to break, while 'shame' is a more intense feeling that you've broken an important major rule.

commentaries.quote: Embarrassment is a form of social pain.
When we get embarrassed, we want to hide. Just crawl into a hole. The fear of judgment and rejection can eat away at our psyche until isolation seems like the only option.
Being embarrassed means that you're human, and we like you better for it.
The best way to handle awkward moments is to gracefully move on, and, if possible, try to find humor in the situation.
